newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Opectra says has Elf plans.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Opectra says has Elf plans.

text.p: Israeli real estate company Opectra Ltd has reached an understanding with France's Elf Aquitaine to set up a network of filling stations in Israel, Opectra managing director Sioma Simon said.
But an Elf spokesman in Paris denied the company planned to enter the Israeli market
Despite the denial, Simon said he stood by his statement. "We hope to have a final agreement with Elf by the end of the year," he said.
Opectra is a real estate company which also has interests in several filling stations.

Simon said talks have been taking place with Elf officials over the past few months. He said the two companies are discussing setting up 20 filling stations over the next two years with an investment of "tens of millions of dollars."
No major international fuel company has a presence in the Israeli market. Until the 1950s Royal Dutch/Shell had a stake in Paz Oil Co, Israel's largest petrol distributor.

Simon said the refined products for the gas stations would come from either Europe or Saudi Arabia. He also said the two companies were looking into the feasibility of importing Saudi crude and refining it at a refinery in the Mediterranean port of Ashkelon. Saudi Arabia has no diplomatic ties with Israel.
Elf denied it was looking into the refinery project in Ashkelon.
